name: Box-Jenkins gas furnace (series J)
license_or_terms: US Government work (NIST), public domain; original data Box, Jenkins & Reinsel
expected_relation: Methane feed rate (input) drives CO2 concentration (output) through a transfer function with a pure dead time; correlation is NEGATIVE (more gas -> less CO2 %).
expected_delay: dead time b=3 samples (27 s); cross-correlation peak at lag 5 samples (45 s) in our check (r=-0.95)
reference: Box, Jenkins & Reinsel (1994) Time Series Analysis, 3rd ed., ch. 11 (series J, transfer model b=3); NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook section 6.4.5.1 (pmc451)
preprocessing_notes: BELOW the 500-sample minimum (296). CSV parsed from NIST .dat (original kept as engineering_gas_furnace.dat, 25-line header). No time column: t_index * 9 s. No NaNs. gas_rate in ft3/min (centered), co2_pct in %.

name: Nino3.4 SST anomaly vs GISTEMP global land-ocean temperature
license_or_terms: NOAA ERSSTv5 (table by B. McNoldy) and NASA GISTEMP v4: US Government data, public domain
expected_relation: El Nino warming in the central Pacific is followed by global-mean surface warming (positive correlation).
expected_delay: ~3 months (temperature lags ENSO by 2-4 months); our check on 10-yr-detrended LOTI: peak at +3 months, r=0.46
reference: Trenberth, Caron, Stepaniak & Worley (2002) JGR 107(D8):4065 doi:10.1029/2000JD000298; Foster & Rahmstorf (2011) Environ. Res. Lett. 6:044022
preprocessing_notes: Inner join on month start (1880-01..2022-12). date parses as datetime. -99.99 converted to NaN: NINO34_ANOM has 1 NaN (2022-12), ONI 2 NaN. LOTI is anomaly in degC with strong warming trend - detrend (e.g. subtract 10-yr running mean) before TDS. NINO34_ANOM uses 30-yr sliding climatology.

name: airGR catchment L0123003, hourly rainfall-runoff
license_or_terms: GPL-2 (airGR R package, INRAE); real French catchment data with anonymised code
expected_relation: Catchment precipitation produces a delayed, smoothed streamflow response (unit hydrograph); positive correlation.
expected_delay: positive, several hours (catchment response time); our check: xcorr peak at +8 h (r=0.50)
reference: Coron et al. (2017) Environ. Model. Softw. 94:166-171 (airGR); rainfall-runoff lag concept: Beven (2012) Rainfall-Runoff Modelling, 2nd ed.
preprocessing_notes: 2004-01-01 00:00 to 2008-12-31 23:00; datetime parses. No NaN in precip/q; temp_c entirely NaN (ignore). precip is intermittent (many zeros) - consider smoothing/log. q_ls = discharge in L/s, q_mm = depth over catchment.

name: airGR catchment L0123001, daily rainfall-runoff
expected_relation: Daily basin rainfall leads daily streamflow (positive).
expected_delay: 0-3 days; our check: xcorr peak at +2 days (r=0.32)
reference: Coron et al. (2017) Environ. Model. Softw. 94:166-171
preprocessing_notes: 1984-01-01..2012-12-31; q_mm has 802 NaN (q_ls 772) - interpolate or segment. Also has temp_c and pet_mm.

name: Victoria (Australia) half-hourly electricity demand vs Melbourne temperature
license_or_terms: tsibbledata R package (GPL-3); data from AEMO and Australian BoM
expected_relation: Temperature drives demand via heating/cooling (U-shaped); in summer heat drives air-conditioning load with lag from building thermal inertia (positive).
expected_delay: ~0.5-1 h in summer after removing the mean diurnal profile (our check DJF: peak +2 samples = 1 h, r=0.68); multi-day cumulative heat effects also documented
reference: Hyndman & Fan (2010) IEEE Trans. Power Systems 25(2):1142-1153; Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3rd ed. (vic_elec)
preprocessing_notes: 2012-01-01..2014-12-31 local; Time is UTC ISO string. No NaNs, regular 30-min. Relation is nonlinear: use summer months (Dec-Feb) or |T-18C|, and remove diurnal/weekly cycles first, otherwise raw xcorr peaks at a spurious -1 h.

name: Beijing US-Embassy PM2.5 with weather (hourly)
license_or_terms: UCI ML Repository "Beijing PM2.5 Data", CC BY 4.0
expected_relation: Sustained (northerly) wind ventilates the basin and lowers PM2.5 (negative); humid stagnant air (high DEWP) accompanies accumulation.
expected_delay: unknown sign only: negative, wind leads by ~0-several hours (our check: peak +1 h, r=-0.25)
preprocessing_notes: 2010-01-01..2014-12-31; time from year/month/day/hour columns (no single datetime). pm2.5 has 2067 NaN (incl. first 24 h). Iws is CUMULATED wind speed (m/s, resets when direction cbwd changes) - consider using diff or log. PM2.5 ug/m3, heavy-tailed: log-transform.

name: Jena climate (MPI-BGC) hourly
license_or_terms: Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry Jena weather station; distributed by Keras/TensorFlow for research/education
expected_relation: Relative humidity moves opposite to air temperature at fixed vapour content (Clausius-Clapeyron), strongly on the diurnal cycle (negative).
expected_delay: ~0 h (near-instantaneous; useful as a zero-lag control); our check: peak 0 h, r=-0.57
reference: Clausius-Clapeyron / diurnal RH cycle: Wallace & Hobbs (2006) Atmospheric Science, 2nd ed.; dataset: Chollet, Deep Learning with Python (Jena climate)
preprocessing_notes: 2009-01-01..2016-12-31; "Date Time" parses with format %d.%m.%Y %H:%M:%S; a few irregular steps (8 gaps of 70-80 min). No NaNs but wv/max. wv contain -9999 sentinels (3 rows in hourly file). Columns: p (mbar), T (degC), Tdew, rh (%), VPdef etc.

name: WTI crude spot vs US regular retail gasoline (weekly)
license_or_terms: EIA data, US Government public domain; datasets/oil-prices ODC-PDDL
expected_relation: Crude oil price changes pass through to retail gasoline prices with a lag (asymmetric "rockets and feathers"); positive.
expected_delay: ~1-2 weeks for the main response, full pass-through 4-8 weeks; our check on weekly differences: lag0 r=0.55 (includes 3-day Fri->Mon offset), lag+1 r=0.39 vs reverse lag r=0.18
reference: Borenstein, Cameron & Gilbert (1997) Q. J. Econ. 112(1):305-339
preprocessing_notes: 1990-08-20..2024-02-05 Monday retail dates; WTI is the weekly average for the week ending the preceding Friday (merge_asof backward, 3-day offset; 13 rows 10 days because of missing WTI weeks). retail has 6 NaN (1990-12-10..1991-01-14). Prices non-stationary: use log-differences. Retail source is a personal GitHub repo holding an unmodified EIA download (header rows retained) - EIA itself is blocked.
